# v1.2.0

`skill_management` gives every installed OpenCode skill a switch: list what is installed, find out
why one will not load, hide it from the model, and put it back. Disabling writes **one** global
`skill` permission rule — no skill file is ever moved, edited or deleted.

**No breaking changes in 1.2.0.** The four actions, their inputs, the JSON envelope, the written
rule shape, the same-line marker and the single-file layout are unchanged since 1.1.0.

## Fixed since v1.1.0

- **`list` no longer reports "N skills differ across other agents" on every call.**
  `summary.diverged` counted hidden internal agents (`title`, `summary`, …), which carry
  `{*,*,deny}`; on a real machine that made every skill look divergent (33/33) and added a noise
  warning to each `list`. Only **visible** agents are compared now; `inspect.agents[]` still lists
  every agent, so the detail is not lost.
- **Frontmatter booleans no longer contradict each other.** `disable-model-invocation: "false"` is a
  string, and `Boolean("false") === true`, so `inspect` reported it as `true` while `list` reported
  `autoinvoke: false` for the same file. `true/yes/on/1` and `false/no/off/0` (quoted or not) are
  normalized now, and both fields go through the same rule.
- **A failed sidecar write no longer turns a successful config change into an error.** Once the
  config was written and verified, a sidecar write failure used to surface as `internal_error`: the
  file really changed, but the result had no `changed` / `diff`. It now returns `ok: true`,
  `changed: true`, keeps `diff`, sets `sidecar: null`, and explains itself in `warnings`. The config
  change is not rolled back.
- **`enable` is no longer blocked by an unrelated file's syntax error.** It reads sidecar-recorded
  config files alongside the target; before, any of them failing to parse plus "no candidate rule"
  produced `config_unparsable`. The hard refusal now applies only to the **target** config file;
  other files are reported in `warnings` by name.

## Also since v1.1.0

- **The installer checks before writing.** If `opencode.json(c)` already lists this package in
  `plugins`, or a second copy sits in `plugins/`, it refuses and exits with code `2`, leaving every
  file untouched — two sources make the host report `Duplicate plugin ID` and fail one of them.
- New installer flags: `--check` / `--dry-run`, `--uninstall` (deletes only this plugin's file),
  `--npm` (asserts the npm channel, never writes), `--force`, `--json`. `<config>` resolves the way
  the host resolves it (`$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` first).
- The plugin exports `PLUGIN_VERSION`, asserted against `package.json` by the harness.
- The acceptance harness grew from 260 to **326 assertions**, and now validates every action's
  `output` against the declared JSON Schema (required fields, property types, `error.code` /
  `error.message`) and asserts that `content` is the same data as `output`.
- README is down to 51 lines; field tables, installer flags, package contents, usage and the test
  workflow moved to the documentation site.
- The documentation site gained **Design decisions** (why permission rules instead of policies, why
  there is no `allow`, why global-only, why text edits plus a same-line marker, why the sidecar is
  only an audit trail — each with its cost) and **Development & verification** (harness sections,
  CI, the performance and release gates, npm package contents, why two copies cannot coexist).
  The **Permissions** page now expands Effects into a `deny` vs `ask` comparison with three real
  skill examples. English and Chinese stay mirrored.

# v1.1.0

`skill_management` gives every installed OpenCode skill a switch: list what is installed, find out
why one will not load, hide it from the model, and put it back. Disabling writes **one** global
`skill` permission rule — no skill file is ever moved, edited or deleted.

## Breaking change in 1.1.0

All four actions now return **one JSON object** instead of Markdown. The tool also declares an
`output` JSON Schema, so the host validates every result; this is a real structured tool result,
not Markdown wrapped in a JSON string.

- Envelope: `schemaVersion` (currently `1`), `action`, `ok`, `warnings`.
- Failures use `ok: false` plus `error: { code, message }`; success is no longer inferred from
  ✅ / ❌ in the text.
- `list` returns `callerAgent`, `summary`, `skills[]`, `config`, `sidecar`, `consistency`.
  `description` is still the first line, no longer truncated to 60 characters.
- `inspect` returns `skill`, `idDerivation`, `agents[]`, `caller`, `conclusion`. Missing and
  ambiguous targets use `skill_not_found` / `name_ambiguous`.
- `disable` / `enable` return `changed`, `reason`, `before`, `diff`, `verification`, `backup`,
  `sidecar`; `enable` also returns `location`, `rule`, `candidates`, `relatedRules`.
- `enable` now returns `ok: false` with `config_unparsable` when the target config cannot be
  parsed and no candidate rule exists, instead of claiming "nothing to change".

Nothing else broke: actions, input fields, the written rule shape, the same-line marker format
and the single-file layout are unchanged.

## Also since v1.0.0

- New bilingual documentation site (Astro + Starlight; English at the root, Chinese under
  `/zh-cn`): <https://sogeisetsu.github.io/opencode-skill-management/>
- README now documents the minimal npm install (`opencode plugin add`) and the package contents.
- Theme/language menus, card alignment and mobile spacing fixes on the docs site.

## What it does

| Action | What you get | Writes config |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | Every registered skill and its effective state for the **calling agent** (`available` / `disabled` / `ask`) | No |
| `inspect` | Why one skill is (not) usable: the matched rule, per-agent differences, how the id was derived | No |
| `disable` | Hidden from the model-visible list and rejected at load (`effect: "ask"` keeps it listed with confirmation) | Yes |
| `enable` | Deletes the one blocking rule, whoever wrote it | Yes |

Permissions are evaluated for the **calling agent only**: last match wins (`findLast`, with `*`
and `?` globs), and **no match falls back to `ask`, not `allow`**.

The rule `disable` writes is exactly this line (the trailing comment is the provenance marker
`enable` uses):

```jsonc
{ "action": "skill", "resource": "windows-shell", "effect": "deny" } // skill_management
```

Writes are atomic, preserve indentation, key order, line endings (CRLF/LF) and BOM, keep one
backup, and are verified by reloading the host and polling the caller's rule set; a write the
host did not pick up is rolled back.

## Usage

```text
skill_management({ action: "list" })
skill_management({ action: "inspect", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", dryRun: true })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", effect: "ask" })
skill_management({ action: "enable",  id: "windows-shell" })
```

A `list` result looks like this (abridged):

```json

  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "action": "list",
  "ok": true,
  "warnings": [],
  "callerAgent": { "id": "build", "verified": true },
  "summary": { "total": 29, "disabled": 1, "ask": 0, "diverged": 2, "derivedIds": 0 },
  "skills": [
    { "id": "windows-shell", "state": "available", "source": "config", "path": "..." },
    { "id": "pdf-tools", "state": "disabled", "source": "catalog", "path": "..." }
  ],

## What this is

`skill_management` adds a switchboard for the skills installed in your OpenCode setup: see what is installed, find out why one will not load, take one out of the model's view, and put it back.

Disabling never touches skill files. It writes **one** `skill` permission rule into your global config (`effect: "deny"`, or `"ask"` for a soft disable). Nothing is deleted, moved or rewritten, and removing that rule restores the skill exactly as it was.

This is the first stable release: the surface described below is frozen for 1.x.

## What it does

| Action | What it does | Writes config |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | Every registered skill with its effective state for the calling agent (`available` / `disabled` / `ask`) | no |
| `inspect` | Why one skill is (un)available: the matching rule, per-agent differences, how its id was derived | no |
| `disable` | Hide it from the model and reject loading it (`effect: "ask"` keeps it listed and asks on load) | yes |
| `enable` | Remove the blocking rule again, whoever wrote it | yes |

How a permission is resolved: the host reads the rule set of **the agent that is calling**, takes the last match (`findLast`) with `*` / `?` globs, and — when nothing matches — falls back to `ask`, not `allow`. That is why `list` and `inspect` evaluate per agent and name the agent they used.

`disable` writes exactly this line (the trailing comment is the origin marker that `enable` uses):

```jsonc
{ "action": "skill", "resource": "windows-shell", "effect": "deny" } // skill_management
```

With `deny` the skill disappears from the model-visible skill list, and loading it through the built-in `skill` tool is rejected (`permission.rejected`).

## How to use

```text
skill_management({ action: "list" })
skill_management({ action: "inspect", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell" })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", dryRun: true })
skill_management({ action: "disable", id: "windows-shell", effect: "ask" })
skill_management({ action: "enable",  id: "windows-shell" })
```

- `id` is the primary key from the host registry; `name` works as an alias when it is unambiguous (an ambiguous name returns candidates, never a guess).
- `dryRun: true` prints the exact lines that would be written and writes nothing.
- Writes are atomic (`.tmp` + rename) and preserve indentation, key order, line endings (CRLF/LF) and BOM. One backup is kept under `<config>/skill_management.backups/` — it is a full copy of the config, which may contain credentials, so delete it if you keep secrets there.
- After writing, the tool reloads the host and **polls** the agent rule sets to confirm the change actually landed; if it did not, the file is rolled back.
- `enable` removes the one blocking rule for that id — it does not have to be a rule this tool wrote. It refuses, and shows you the rule, when it cannot uniquely identify it, or when the blocker is a wildcard rule, an agent-level `permissions` entry, or a policy (those are only reported, never edited).

## What's changed since v0.2.0

**Fixed — `disable` with `effect: "ask"` could report success without doing anything.** The read-back check asked "is the caller's effective effect *not* deny?". The host falls back to `ask` when no rule matches, and an agent's own rule can sit *after* the global one and turn it into `allow` — neither is `deny`, so the check passed even when the host had never loaded the rule. It now verifies that the number of matching `{ skill, id, ask }` rules in the caller's rule set actually went up (`0 → 1` appears in the output). If the rule was loaded but a later agent rule overrides it, the output says so instead of claiming it took effect.

**Fixed — a single-line `permissions` array produced invalid JSON.** With `"permissions": [{ … }]` all on one line, adding a rule put the comma *after* the new entry, leaving a config the host could not parse. Insertion now handles the one-line case.

## What this is

`skill_management` puts a control panel on the skills installed in your OpenCode setup. It can list them, explain why one is unavailable, hide one from the model, and bring it back.

Disabling never touches skill files: it writes a single `skill` permission rule into your global config (`effect: "deny"`, or `"ask"` for a soft disable). Nothing is deleted, moved or rewritten, and removing the rule restores the skill exactly as it was.

| Action | What it does | Writes config |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | Every registered skill with its effective state for the calling agent (`available` / `disabled` / `ask`) | no |
| `inspect` | Why one skill is (un)available: the matching rule, per-agent differences, how its id was derived | no |
| `disable` | Hide it from the model and reject loading it (`effect: "ask"` keeps it listed and asks on load) | yes |
| `enable` | Remove the blocking rule again, whoever wrote it | yes |

Install in one command: `opencode plugin add github:sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management` (details below).

## What's changed since v0.1.0

**Fixed — `list` reported the wrong state.** It merged every agent's permission rules before evaluating them, so deny rules owned by sub-agents (`explorer`, `title`, …) leaked into the caller's result: on a stock setup 28 of 29 skills showed up as `disabled` while `inspect` said they were available. States are now evaluated against the calling agent only — the output names that agent, and adds a one-line hint when other agents disagree (which is normal for sub-agents that deny everything).

**Added — one-command verification on Linux / WSL.** `tools/linux-verify.sh` puts Node and the OpenCode CLI in a temporary directory under `$HOME`, runs the full acceptance suite (175 assertions), confirms a real OpenCode host loads the plugin, then cleans up after itself. No `sudo`, no writes to your real config.

**Docs — README rewritten for users.** It now leads with the problem the tool solves and explains the four actions (`list` / `inspect` / `disable` / `enable`): what each one does, when to reach for it, and whether it writes configuration.

**Verified.** 175 assertions pass on Windows and on Linux (Debian 13.5, OpenCode 2.0.32). The `disable → rejected load → enable` round trip was re-run on a Linux host: the skill disappears from the model-visible list, loading it is rejected, and `enable` restores it.

## Install or upgrade

```pwsh
# via git (no registry, no token)
opencode plugin add github:sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management

# via npm
opencode plugin add opencode-skill-management@0.2.0
```

**Offline / single file:** download `skill_management.js` from the assets below and drop it into `<config>/plugins/`. The `opencode-skill-management-0.2.0.tgz` asset is the exact npm tarball if you prefer to unpack it yourself.

Confirm it is loaded:

```pwsh
opencode plugin list --builtin
# skill_management   local   <config>/plugins/skill_management.js
```

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/sogeisetsu/opencode-skill-management/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0
